claim: Splitting a proof into symbolic sub-goals helps a language-model prover only if the prover can discharge nearly all of them, because one unproved obligation leaves the whole proof incomplete. Supported only if giving the Wilf-Zeilberger decomposition to an untrained general prover adds no end-to-end proofs, with that prover proving under half of the sub-goal lemmas and completing none of the decomposed identities, whereas with the specialised prover lemma accuracy exceeds 70% and most decomposed identities are completed; and if on benchmarks where few problems fit the method the decomposition adds at most a few proofs.

experiments: Build the decomposition and the benchmark. Setup: normalise each Lean statement to a canonical summation form (shift ranges, rewrite bounded sums, split parity cases); for identities the Wilf-Zeilberger method covers, have SageMath synthesise the rational certificate and generate Lean obligations: the recurrence lemma, boundary terms, non-vanishing side conditions for denominators, normalisation lemmas and case branches; identities it does not cover become direct proving targets. Benchmark LCI-Test: 100 identities from two classical collections reserved for testing, with canonical forms checked to be absent from training. Success means the whole proof is accepted by the Lean 4 kernel within 32 attempts.

Give the decomposition to the untrained prover. Setup: the same Wilf-Zeilberger sub-goals discharged by Goedel-Prover-V2 instead of the specialised prover, pass@32. Result: 9/100 on LCI-Test, identical to Goedel-Prover-V2 without decomposition; 13/100 on CombiBench (one more) and 0/36 on PutnamBench-Comb (no change).

Diagnose at the level of lemmas. Setup: the 1,178 sub-goals produced for the 46 LCI-Test identities the method decomposes, attempted by each prover. Result: Goedel-Prover-V2 proves 564 (47.88%) and completes 0 of 46 identities; the specialised prover proves 864 (73.34%) and completes 29 of 46. On CombiBench and PutnamBench-Comb, where few problems are identities of this type, the decomposition route contributes only 1 proof each.
